beats.say: Nearly twenty billion tiny switches are flipping inside your phone. Right now.
beats.caption: Nearly 20 billion tiny switches are flipping inside your phone. Right now.

beats.say: But they have zero moving parts. So how do they switch?
beats.caption: But they have ZERO moving parts. So how do they switch?

beats.say: Zoom in. Past the metal lid. Into the silicon.
Each switch is a transistor. Over a thousand could line up across one human hair.
beats.caption: Each switch is a transistor. Over 1,000 could line up across one human hair.

beats.say: It has three parts. A source. A drain. And a gate.
No voltage on the gate? Electrons can't cross. That's a zero.
Now add voltage. A channel opens, and electrons rush through. That's a one!
Quick, guess. How many times per second can it flip? Comment your number.
Wire a few together and you get logic. Logic becomes math. And math becomes every photo, every game, every message you've ever sent.
